about: The mutant ledger of the IR build path's coverage and agreement tooling (internal/experimental/irspike and the IR builder's census in internal/sketch/lower/ir.go). Its killers need the IR toolchains or the full tier; see toolchain/ir/ports.md. The patch-level mutant port-stock-not-identical (a planted codegen change outside the -ergoir guard) is an edit of the Go patch, run with scripts/irport -patch, not here. TestIRRuntimeChecks (race detector, GC checkmark) was deleted in batch-18 fix-tool: it guarded only the derivative's stack and pointer maps, and no mutant of this repository reached it.

mutants.name: ir-try-no-propagate
mutants.from: Then: []*irStmt{{K: k, Pos: p, X: errLocal}}}
mutants.to: Then: []*irStmt{{K: k, Pos: p, X: errLocal}}[:0]}
mutants.rule: A try leaves the frame with the callee's error; it never goes on with a zero value

mutants.name: ir-catch-default-swallows
mutants.from: sw.Else = []*irStmt{{K: k, Pos: sw.ElsePos, X: &irExpr{K: "local", Pos: sw.ElsePos, I: e}}}
mutants.to: sw.Else = []*irStmt{{K: k, Pos: sw.ElsePos, X: &irExpr{K: "local", Pos: sw.ElsePos, I: e}}}[:0]
mutants.rule: A total catch's default arm panics with the error; it never returns it

mutants.name: ir-catch-else-dropped
mutants.from: ifs.Else = []*irStmt{{K: "set", Pos: sw.End, Local: result, X: &irExpr{K: "local", Pos: sw.End, I: v}}}
mutants.to: ifs.Else = []*irStmt{{K: "set", Pos: sw.End, Local: result, X: &irExpr{K: "local", Pos: sw.End, I: v}}}[:0]
mutants.rule: A catch with no error takes the call's value; the success branch sets the result

mutants.name: ir-spill-skipped
mutants.rule: An operand before one that runs statements is evaluated first, into a temporary (callArgs order)

mutants.name: ir-loop-poll-dropped
mutants.rule: A polling frame's loop polls the task at the end of each iteration (loopBody)

mutants.name: ir-fail-as-panic
mutants.rule: A failure return in a fallible frame fails it; it panics only in a frame that cannot fail

mutants.name: ir-catch-arm-swapped
mutants.rule: Each catch case runs its own arm's body

mutants.name: ir-env-last
mutants.rule: An impure callee takes the environment first, after a method's receiver (callText)

mutants.name: ir-hoist-skipped
mutants.rule: An effectful call in value position runs into a temporary before its expression, so it never overtakes an earlier operand (the emitter's v := f(…))

mutants.name: ir-unit-tail-dropped
mutants.rule: A body with no value whose tail is an error value fails with it (retExpr); the value is never dropped

mutants.name: irt-ir-tests-skip
mutants.rule: The full tier runs the IR tests with ergo's own toolchains when no variable names them; it never skips them silently.

mutants.name: ir-text-not-overlaid
mutants.rule: The Go text view holds the printed IR bodies, not the declarations without bodies

mutants.name: irspike-unary-dropped
mutants.from: return &irExpr{K: "un", Pos: p, Op: op, X: b.expr(x.X)}
mutants.rule: An IR unary expression keeps its operator (! and -): the IR path prints what the source path prints. Only the generated programs hold a unary operator; the kernel has none.

mutants.name: irspike-ir-line-shifted
mutants.rule: An IR node carries its .ergo line, so the derivative reports an IR body that does not check at the source position.

mutants.name: irspike-ir-name-not-content
mutants.origin: wf10 batch-18 fix-tool (verify M2, the IR1 request's M5)
mutants.rule: The -ergoir flag, the one key of the IR in Go's build cache, names the IR file's content, not the module it was written in: an edit of the IR alone, in the same module, builds again (each seed of TestIRMatchesSource writes its own module, so only this test sees the difference).

mutants.name: irt-split-case-dropped
mutants.rule: The parts of a split run every target of the examples once: a split never leaves a target out.

mutants.name: irt-split-part-missing
mutants.rule: Every part of a split is a test function; a missing one leaves its targets unrun.

mutants.name: irt-split-duplicate-target
mutants.rule: A folder's test build is one target, though ExampleTargets lists it again after a subfolder: each target builds and runs once.
